mathematical_route: Actual level calibration: finite-area indicators are L2-admissible, signed coarea gaps are nonnegative and integrate to zero. Hence almost every signed level minimizes globally in the selected branch, with energy zero. This supplies global radial-cut admissibility; compact-perturbation curvature alone is not used to justify unbounded tail removal.

Ball calculus: polar Fubini plus scalar differentiation for indicator radial slices gives an actual L1 sphere trace for almost every radius. The smooth product identity D(fh)=hDf+f grad h dx then gives exact inside/outside derivative measures, with mutually singular bulk and sphere terms. The same local calculation gives complement cuts and relative-domain formulas. Sphere arclength is explicitly normalized.

Removal and filling comparisons give P(E cap B)<=2s_E+integral(E cap B)k and P((U minus E) cap B)<=2s_complement-integral(complement cap B)k. For full-space global minimizers, comparison with E cap B also gives the outside-cut inequality. All compared indicators have actually proved finite area/perimeter.

Perimeter submodularity is proved by mollifying both indicators and applying a smooth min/max approximation with complementary convex gradient weights. The obstacle comparison then extends the signed Dirichlet field by the fixed exterior lower bound g, including balls meeting the domain boundary.

Uniform local inequalities use strongly convergent exact fields and a global L2 noise bound, with the strict prescribed thresholds. Neumann uses the exact indicator Sobolev-Poincare expression, plus a finite-chart Lipschitz exterior rectangle at ambient points on the domain boundary. The false relative-complement density bound for E=Omega is not imported.

Full-space support uses no component/Jordan decomposition: empty comparison plus inside/tail splitting and isoperimetry give sqrt(|E|)<=C/gamma and P(E)<=2sqrt(pi)C/gamma. The outside-ball volume A obeys gamma sqrt(A)<=-2A', giving extinction by R+4sqrt(A(R))/gamma<=R+4C/gamma^2. Zero exterior volume implies the density-one representative and its topological boundary are supported in the common closed ball.

The required square-root integration is proved directly for the actual monotone integral volumes by finite partitions and the scalar mean value theorem. The DC-dependent general converse absolutely-continuous FTC is not a supplier; original Countable Choice is preserved.

The limiting minimum-norm exact dual field calibrates every selected minimum-TV exact solution by the adjoint identity and equality of minimum TV. Thus the same density/support constants apply to the selected limit. Global L1 convergence, almost-everywhere level measure convergence, and both Hausdorff directions are then proved, including empty-level conventions and nonunique exact solutions.
